title: Unique Email Addresses
description: Every valid email address consists of a local name and a domain name separated by `'@'`. In the local name, periods `'.'` are ignored, and everything from the first `'+'` onward is ignored (these rules do not apply to the domain name). Given an array of valid email strings `emails`, return the number of distinct canonical addresses that actually receive mail.
constraints: Each email contains exactly one '@' with non-empty local and domain parts.
hints: Split each email at '@': keep the domain verbatim.
In the local part, truncate at the first '+' (if any), remove all '.', then insert local + '@' + domain into a set.

examples.explanation: The first two emails normalize to "testemail@leetcode.com" and the third to "testemail@lee.tcode.com", giving 2 unique addresses.
All three addresses have different local names, giving 3.
Dots and plus-tags in the local name normalize all three to "user@domain.com".
